newsitem.title: SPAIN: BBV H1 profit up 26 pct as Latam investments shine.
newsitem.headline: BBV H1 profit up 26 pct as Latam investments shine.

text.p: Banco Bilbao Vizcaya reported on Thursday that its first-half net profit rose 25.9 percent, as both basic banking and Latin American investments performed well.
Net attributable profit climbed to 58.11 billion pesetas ($378.4 million) from 46.15 billion a year earlier, with strong gains registered in core bank lending and fee income and in Latin America.
"The increase in BBV results is based principally on ordinary business," chairman Emilio Ybarra told reporters. "All sources of revenue increased intensely."
Profits from its Latin American operations provided 30 percent of its total profit, a "decisive" contribution, he said.
Net interest income, which reflects revenues from lending and the costs of interest-bearing deposits, rose 32.6 percent to 265.44 billion pesetas.
Ordinary revenue, which also reflects commission and trading revenues, rose 35.8 percent to 393.19 billion pesetas. Non-recurring items contributed just eight percent to earnings, Ybarra said.
"In Spain, the environment is developing favourably although there is pressure on bank margins," Ybarra said.
BBV forecast that lending would rise 11 to 12 percent this year as the Spanish economy recuperated and consumer spending accelerated. Lending rose 8.4 percent last year.

BBV has been capitalising on new Latin American investments, taking advantage of the high growth and margins that will compensate for falling domestic margins and for the potential loss of business tied to the launch of the euro set for 1999.

After an aggressive 1996 shopping spree, BBV has acquired 40 percent of Provincial in Venezuela and 71.7 percent of Credito Argentino this year. As of May, it had assets of 3.9 trillion pesetas and 1,150 offices in Latin America.

"Latin America is the star in the presentation of results," said Jose Ignacio Goerigolzarri, who handles Latin America for the bank. "We want to complete our presence and constitute our group in Latin America."
Excluding write-downs for goodwill and financing costs, Latin America contributed 30.67 billion pesetas toward pre-tax earnings of 142.92 billion pesetas in the first half.

Including goodwill and financing, overall BBV group pre-tax profit was 129.52 billion pesetas. Latin America provided net interest income of 86.77 billion pesetas and ordinary income of 124.18 billion pesetas.
BBV now plans to strengthen its current investments and does not rule out eventual purchases in Chile and Brazil. "It is clear that BBV is interested in those markets," Goirigolzarri said.
But he said that so far BBV had found no candidates that fit its strategy. "In Chile, the banks we are looking at are very expensive and we are still looking at Brazil as well," he said.
BBV said it would also present a bid soon in the imminent Mexican tender for bank Banpais.
